verses.english: like a rain-cloud in the wet season, thundering with lightning.
Then he turned back, enraged and not his own master.
Having directly known all of that, having surveyed it, the One with vision

verses.pali_roman: Tato āmantayī satthā sāvake sāsane rate:
verses.english: then addressed, as Teacher, the disciples who delight in the teaching:
“Māra's host has come. Know them, bhikkhus.”

verses.pali_roman: Te ca ātappa-makaruṃ sutvā buddhassa sāsanaṃ.
verses.english: And they made an ardent effort, having heard the Buddha's instruction.
From those free of lust it withdrew. Not one hair of theirs was stirred.

verses.pali_roman: Modanti saha bhūtehi sāvakā te jane sutā”ti.

vocabulary.meaning: a rain-cloud of the wet season. The simile for Mara's host arriving, thundering and flashing
not in one's own power. Said of Mara turning back, enraged and no longer master of himself
not even a hair of theirs was stirred — the phrase that measures the disciples' composure against Mara's whole army
one who has won the battle. The sutta's last epithet for the disciples, and its closing image

checks.issue: THE SUTTA AND THE BOOK BOTH END HERE, and NO COLOPHON IS PRINTED. Every Thai-script chant in this book closes with a nitthitam formula; this one simply stops after the last verse, with white paper below it. No closing was written, because inventing one would put a line on the page the book does not print.

TWO WHITE CORRIDORS, x 913-1009 and x 1094-1152, rather than one. The left column's longest lines reach into the space between them, so the single clean gutter the other sheets have does not exist here. The second column's left edge is the reliable measure.

HEAVY BLEED-THROUGH FROM THE REVERSE OF THE SHEET, and it is a DONOR LIST with names and money amounts, not chant text — clearly legible in mirror image across the lower half. It was checked at 3x to be certain none of it is on this side. Nothing from it has been entered, and the lower half of page 325 is genuinely blank.
The book prints 'Tato amantayi sattha' with a LONG i here, where page 319 verse 55 prints the same line with a SHORT i. Both read clearly at 5x. Kept as each page sets it rather than made to agree.

THIS COMPLETES THE MAHASAMAYA SUTTA AND THE BOOK: verses 184-192 finish the chant that opened on page 317, and page 325 is the last printed page. Three findings. (1) NO COLOPHON — the sutta just stops, where every Thai-script chant in this book closes with a nitthitam formula. Nothing was invented to fill it. (2) THE BLEED-THROUGH ON THIS SHEET IS A DONOR LIST, names and amounts from the reverse, legible in mirror across the lower half; checked at 3x and none of it is on this side. (3) 'amantayi' LONG HERE, SHORT ON PAGE 319 — the same line, two spellings, both kept.
